claims.statement: The Workbench has one compact source-backed model for pages, objects, and application navigation.
The missing model is a fourth diagram body declared by type application.
Application Maps own pages, user-visible durable objects, ownership/cardinality, page states, and app-level navigation.
Pages can link explicitly to overview capabilities, flow nodes, wireframe screens, and external planning documents.
The viewer provides a page graph, object rail, page inspector, direct artifact links, source refresh, page/state URL state, and coverage warnings.
Unsafe paths are parser errors; missing, wrong-type, and missing-target cross-file references are non-blocking warnings.
A valid Application Map is the preferred project home, with overview fallback.
Application Maps remain source-backed and read-only in the first slice.
The first slice does not add application variants, a universal graph, in-app editing, a new API route, or a renderer abstraction.
Requirements, tickets, API contracts, database fields, and the full planning corpus remain outside the DSL.
Same-folder discovery and recursive project structure do not create semantic links.
The evidence-first resume studio is the representative proof for the Application Map.
claims.notes: Representative evidence must not become universal resume requirements.

claims.statement: Existing catalog, shell, source-refresh, and typed reference patterns should be reused before new infrastructure is added.

shape.appetite: One medium read-only capability delivered through four small vertical slices with no new dependency.
shape.problem: The Workbench lacks an explicit owner for application pages, conceptual objects, app navigation, and cross-artifact coverage.
shape.recommended_shape: A fourth type application document with pages, objects, ownership/cardinality, navigation, and typed explicit references, rendered by a specialized read-only workbench.
success_moves: Prove the source model before the viewer.
Keep the four reference kinds separate.
Reuse the current read path and catalog.
Keep target failures as non-blocking warnings.
Keep page state in the URL.

first_proof.question: Does a compact Application Map make the resume studio’s page ownership and artifact coverage easier to understand?
first_proof.artifact: One valid resume Application Map loaded through the existing catalog/API path and rendered with page graph, object rail, inspector, and typed links.
first_proof.decision_rule: Continue when explicit semantics, safe references, warning behavior, and existing-document fallbacks all work without inferred relationships.

open_decisions.fallback: Use the smallest explicit line syntax that preserves typed targets.
